insights.topic: Verified purchase cost vs. ad tech CPA
insights.insight: The protocol settles a verified, cryptographically signed purchase event at roughly $0.10 per receipt — compared to $5–$150 CPA charged by probabilistic ad tech stacks. That is not a marginal efficiency gain; it is a structural repricing of what a confirmed conversion costs.

With Chrome cookie deprecation joining Safari and Firefox, the primary cross-site tracking primitive is gone — and device fingerprinting, first-party data, and data brokers all produce signals, not proof. A verified receipt is the only artifact that eliminates the attribution problem rather than approximating around it.

insights.topic: Physical commerce dominance in the signal set
insights.insight: Grocery, Dining, and Gas account for 56% of receipts across two consecutive 14-day observation windows — a structurally stable share, not a sampling artifact. Brands competing in everyday physical categories have a higher-density signal pool here than in digital-first panels.

insights.topic: Walmart concentration and premium grocery entry
insights.insight: Walmart holds 84 of the top brand receipts in the trailing 14-day window; Whole Foods Market entered the brand list for the first time on 2026-03-28. That pairing — mass and premium grocery in the same verified dataset — signals category range expanding beyond value-tier shoppers.

Active coverage spans 21+ CBSAs with documented burst expansion into non-metro AZ, CA, FL, IA, KY, MA, ME, MN, NC, NJ, NV, NY, OH, SC, WI, and WV — not concentrated in top-10 DMAs. The diffusion pattern is consistent with organic social-graph spread, which tends to produce more durable geographic reach than paid campaign rollouts.

The protocol has crossed $400K in verified GMV with no observed deceleration in category mix or geographic coverage across milestone thresholds. At current 7-day run rate ($25,208 GMV, 546 receipts), the dataset is compounding — not plateauing — which matters for brands evaluating whether the signal pool is large enough to act on.
